then.text: Hello again. Mind the oven, and have a slice of gâche on the house. Are you still collecting for the chapel? Marvellous.

For the Little Chapel? Of course. I've a saucer that cracked in the oven, blue and white, a good one. Brother Déodat used to collect broken crockery from every house on the island. A bit of my own was in there before I was born.
Here you are. Give it to the Brother with my love, and tell him he still owes me for the last tray of gâche.

else.text: Gâche, hot out of the oven. Raisins, peel and a lot of butter. You cut it thick and spread it thicker. And if you want something to wash it down, we've a pot of tea going.
The old bakers used to bake everyone's bean jar in the cooling oven on a Saturday night. We keep that spirit alive, at higher prices.
